User: I'm filling out a form that asks for my SSN. My SSN is ***-**-6789 (last four: 4567). Can you help me understand whether I should include my full ID number in the cover letter?
Assistant: Short answer: usually no — don’t put your full SSN in a cover letter. Only give the last four (or say you’ll provide the full number through a secure channel) unless the employer or agency specifically requires the full SSN on that document and tells you how to send it securely.

Why:
- Cover letters are widely share

d and often transmitted by email or uploaded to systems that may not be encrypted — including a full SSN increases risk of identity theft.
- Many organizations only need the last four digits for initial screening. Full SSNs are normally requested later (background check, payroll, tax forms, official application) and via secure methods.

Practical guidance:
- If the form explicitly asks you to include SSN on the cover letter, check the form instructions or contact the recipient to confirm why and how it will

be stored/transmitted.
- Prefer giving only the last four digits in the cover letter (e.g., “Last four digits of SSN: 4567”) or a statement that you will provide the full SSN via a secure channel.
- Never put a full SSN in an email subject line or in an unencrypted email attachment.
- If they require the full SSN, ask to submit it via:
  - A secure online portal (HTTPS) that they specify, or
  - An encrypted attachment, or
  - Over the phone to a verified staff member, or
  - In person when turning in pape

rwork.
- Keep a copy of any directions or confirmation showing why they needed it and how you transmitted it.

Suggested wording you can use in your cover letter:
- Option A (give last four): “For privacy, I’ve included only the last four digits of my Social Security number: 4567. I can provide the full number upon request through a secure channel.”
- Option B (decline to include): “I have not included my full Social Security number in this cover letter. Please let me know the secure method you prefer for p

roviding it.”

If you want, I can:
- Draft a one-line sentence tailored to your cover letter,
- Draft a short email asking the recipient how they prefer to receive the full SSN securely,
- Or review the form instructions if you paste them here.
